summary: Chaim Rabin was a linguist who studied at SOAS University of London and the University of Oxford (Christ Church). He held academic posts at Oxford (1941–1956) and the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (1956–1986).

Chaisit Suwanvarangkul is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He worked as a researcher at Kyoto University and the University of Delhi, and served as a Lecturer in Buddhist Studies at the University of Otago (attested 2015).

Chakravarthi Ram-Prasad specializes in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He earned a doctorate in philosophy from Oxford, held research fellowships at Clare Hall, Cambridge, and Trinity College, Oxford, taught at NUS, and became a Distinguished Professor at Lancaster University.

Chamnong Adivadhanasit works in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned a BA from Chulalongkorn University, where he later served as a part-time instructor (attested 2012), and was a professor of social science at Kasetsart University (attested 2012).

Champa Thupten Zongtse was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served on the faculty at the University of Göttingen, where he is attested from 1991 and worked as a lecturer (attested 2009).

Chan Ju Mun is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Charles Hallisey, Morten Schlütter, and Masahiro Shimoda. He also studied at the University of Tokyo and with John D. Dunne.
Chandima is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara under Uma Shankar Vyas.

Chandrabhāl Tripāṭhī was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at the University of Göttingen under Ernst Waldschmidt. He held posts at Göttingen and the University of Cologne, and served as Professor of Indology at Free University of Berlin.

Chang-geun Hwang is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned his PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 2000. He studied under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, Minoru Kiyota, and Morten Schlütter.

Changhwan Park is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at Otani University under Noritoshi Aramaki and Shoryu Katsura, completed his PhD at UC Berkeley under Alexander von Rospatt, and served as professor at Geumgang University.

Channa Li is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology who studied under Jonathan A. Silk (attested 2015). Li is attested in 2026 as a research fellow at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Chao-heng Liao is a scholar in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He has been affiliated with Academia Sinica (attested 2018) and served as an adjunct researcher at the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Charlene Makley is a Tibetology and religious studies scholar. She earned her PhD from the University of Michigan in 1999 under Norma Diamond and Roy Rappaport, and later became an associate professor of anthropology at Reed College.

Charles A. Moore was a philosopher and Indologist who earned his AB and PhD at Yale University, where he also taught. He conducted postdoctoral work at Banaras Hindu University and was a professor at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (1936–1967).
Charles Alfred Bell was a scholar in Tibetology and linguistics. He completed his education at Winchester College (~1884–1889) and New College (~1889–1891).

Charles B. Jones is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under Paul Groner and served as Associate Professor and Associate Dean at the Catholic University of America.

Charles Bally was a linguist who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin and under Ferdinand de Saussure. He spent his academic career holding a post at the University of Geneva from circa 1893 to 1939.

Charles Burnett is a scholar of history, archaeology, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at the University of Cambridge and held posts at St John's College, the University of Sheffield, and notably the Warburg Institute, where he became a professor in 1999.

Charles Cutler Torrey was a scholar of history, archaeology, religious studies, and linguistics who studied under Theodor Nöldeke. He taught Semitic languages at Andover Theological Seminary (1892–1900) and served as a professor at Yale University (1900–1932).

Charles D. Orzech is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies who completed his dissertation at the University of Chicago. He chaired the Religious Studies Department at the University of North Carolina at Greensboro and was a National Humanities Center Fellow.
